That floor also fixed something I'd left arbitrary — **the volume gate is now derived, not chosen**: λ ≥ 3.7, set exactly so every judged series can move in both directions. 12 of 1,173 rows fall below it.

**Asymmetric α (0.025 low / 0.005 high).** Counts are bounded below and unbounded above, so symmetric α isn't symmetric in practice. Measured result: **19 high / 19 low** — asymmetric input, symmetric output. 0.49 flags/week for a 15-location account.

**A2 — the trimmed mean earns its place on a case I hadn't seen.** Account 6 the week *after* the spike: plain-mean baseline λ=138.0 flags n=102 as **below normal** — a false alarm manufactured by the spike sitting in the next week's baseline. Trimmed λ=72.3 → normal. That's now a named regression test, not just a design note.

**A3, B4, B5, C6, C7, D8, D9, E10** — all applied. φ moved to Deferred. Every worked number recomputed: account 8 is now 7 vs λ=10.8, band [5,20], p=0.157 (the 5.1–15.7 figure is gone, as are 105.0 and 72.7). Three projects, conventions extracted from VerusLLC into CLAUDE.md in T0 — not read before then.

**One thing got worse, and you should see it before approving.** With the corrected model the default week flags **zero** accounts and **zero** locations — not the 2 and 4 I reported under the broken approximation. The page is genuinely empty on arrival. I did *not* fix this by loosening α; instead the location list always ranks by tail probability, so the most unusual site sits at the top whether or not anything is flagged. input.plan:
# DASH-247 — Implementation Plan (rev 2)

## Context

Relay customers see raw totals per location and can't tell whether this week's numbers are
good, bad, or typical. Account managers field "is this normal for us?" by hand; support hears
that multi-location customers can't spot which site needs attention.

Profiling the seed (`tools/profile_seed.py`, 12,626 events / 20 accounts / 26 weeks) produced
one finding that determines the design:

**Weekly counts are statistically indistinguishable from Poisson arrivals.** Fano factor
(variance/mean) is 0.93 median at account grain and 0.93 at location grain.

So the week-to-week "variation" customers stare at is arrival randomness. There is no trend to
read, and spread scales as √λ — the same percentage move means different things at 5 events/week
and 50. The feature is a **volume-aware significance test**, not a chart and not a threshold.

Rev 2 corrects the statistical model: rev 1 used a normal approximation that is invalid at our
volumes. All numbers below are recomputed.

---

## 1. Interpretation of "is this normal for us?"

| | Decision |
|---|---|
| **Test** | **Exact Poisson tail probabilities.** Flag above if `P(X ≥ n \| λ) < 0.005`, below if `P(X ≤ n \| λ) < 0.025`. Computed by a CDF loop in C#, no stats library. |
| **Baseline λ** | **Trimmed mean** of the trailing **12 complete weeks** (min 8): drop the single highest and single lowest, average the remaining 10. |
| **Band** | The integer interval of counts that would not be flagged. Non-negative by construction. |
| **Gate** | λ ≥ 3.7, **derived** (below), not chosen. Under it: `not enough volume`. |
| **Ranking** | Location list sorted by **tail probability**, always — flags are badges on top of the ordering, not the ordering itself. |
| **Window** | Cutoff is the **dataset-wide** `MAX(occurred_at)` = `2026-07-27T22:20:34Z`, converted into each account's local calendar. Not per-account max. |
| **Default view** | Last complete week, `2026-07-20 … 2026-07-26`, with navigation to earlier complete weeks. |
| **Verdicts** | `above normal` / `below normal` / `normal` / `not enough volume`. |

### Why exact tails, not the normal approximation

Rev 1's `λ ± 2.576·√λ` produces a **negative lower bound whenever λ ≤ 6.64**, which is most of our
locations (location-grain λ runs 3.3–11.3). A negative bound means "below normal" is unreachable.
Measured over all 1,173 judged location-weeks, symmetric 99% normal-approx scoring fires
**20 high flags and 0 low flags** — the drop detector never fires once in 25 weeks. That directly
contradicts §2.3 (drops are the more actionable signal).

| λ | exact band | normal-approx 99% lower |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | [0, 8] | −1.46 |
| 4 | [1, 10] | −1.15 |
| 5 | [1, 12] | −0.76 |
| 6 | [2, 13] | −0.31 |
| 8 | [3, 16] | 0.71 |
| 25 | [16, 39] | 12.12 |
| 75 | [59, 98] | 52.69 |

Exact tails give a non-negative integer band at every λ. Verified: **0 of 1,173** location-weeks
produce `lo < 0` or `hi < lo`.

### Smallest λ at which a drop to zero is detectable

A location observing **zero** events is flagged below only when `e^(−λ) < α_low`:

| α_low | λ must exceed |
|---|---|
| 0.005 | **5.30** |
| 0.010 | 4.61 |
| **0.025** | **3.69** |
| 0.050 | 3.00 |

This is an information limit, not a tunable: below that λ, no observation however low is
distinguishable from chance. **The gate is set at λ ≥ 3.7 precisely so that every judged series
can move in both directions.** Only 12 of 1,173 location-weeks fall below it.

### Why asymmetric α (0.025 low / 0.005 high)

Counts are bounded below at zero and unbounded above, so a symmetric α is not symmetric in
practice. The cost is also asymmetric: a missed drop is lost business, a false spike is noise.
Measured across all judged location-weeks:

| α (low/high) | flag rate | high / low | 15-location account |
|---|---|---|---|
| .005 / .005 | 1.71% | 20 / **0** | 0.26/wk |
| .010 / .005 | 2.22% | 20 / 6 | 0.33/wk |
| **.025 / .005** | **3.27%** | **19 / 19** | **0.49/wk — 1 per 2 weeks** |
| .025 / .025 | 5.20% | 42 / 19 | 0.78/wk |
| .050 / .010 | 5.54% | 26 / 39 | 0.83/wk |

Asymmetric input, symmetric output: 19 high and 19 low. One flagged location per fortnight for a
15-location account is a triage list, not alert fatigue.

### Why a trimmed mean, not "exclude detected anomalies"

Rev 1 said "exclude detected anomaly weeks", which is circular — detection depends on the
baseline that detection is supposed to clean. The trimmed mean is unconditional and needs no
detector. It is not cosmetic; concrete case, account 6 the week **after** the spike:

| | baseline λ | verdict for n=102 |
|---|---|---|
| plain mean | 138.0 | **below normal — false alarm** |
| trimmed mean | 72.3 | normal |

The spike sits in the following week's baseline window and, untrimmed, nearly doubles λ and
manufactures a drop that did not happen. Trimming also leaves the spike's own detection intact:
for week `2026-06-01`, λ = 72.1, band [56, 95], n = 880 → **above normal**.

### Worked examples (last complete week, recomputed)

| series | n | λ | band | p | verdict | a % rule says |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| acct 8 | 7 | 10.80 | [5, 20] | p_low 0.157 | normal | −35%, alarm |
| acct 19 | 13 | 8.60 | [3, 17] | p_high 0.097 | normal | +51%, alarm |
| acct 15 / Site B | 2 | 6.80 | [2, 14] | p_low 0.034 | normal, at the band floor | −71%, alarm |
| acct 6, `2026-06-01` | 880 | 72.10 | [56, 95] | p_high ≈ 0 | **above normal** | correct by luck |

Account 15 / Site B is the honest case: a 71% drop with p = 0.034 is suggestive but not separable
from chance across 15 locations. It is not flagged — and it still surfaces, because the list ranks
by tail probability and it sorts second out of 69. **This is why ranking matters more than
flagging**: the page is useful in weeks when nothing crosses a threshold.

### Alternatives considered and rejected

**A. Percent change vs a trailing average (flag ±20%).** Rejected: wrong at these volumes. Three
of the four rows above are large percentage moves that are ordinary weeks. With spread ∝ √λ, a
fixed percentage is far too tight for small locations and too loose for large ones.

**B. Median/MAD modified z-score** (what `profile_seed.py` uses for discovery). Right tool for
finding outliers offline, wrong for a per-request band on small counts: MAD over 12 small integers
is typically 1 or 2, so the band moves in coarse discrete jumps. Robustness is supplied instead by
the trimmed mean.

---

## 2. Open questions for product

| # | Question | Working assumption |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Normal vs the account's own history, or vs industry peers? | **Own history.** Peer benchmarking is a different product. |
| 2 | Is "activity" all events, or judged per type? | **Total events**; per-type split shown for context. A location can hold totals flat while appointments collapse — a real gap. |
| 3 | Are drops as important as spikes? | **More so.** Encoded as α_low = 5× α_high. Worth confirming the cost ratio is right. |
| 4 | Is 1 flag per fortnight per 15-location account the right noise budget? | **Yes.** Directly tunable via the α table in §1 if product disagrees. |
| 5 | New accounts have no verdict for their first 8 complete weeks. Acceptable? | **Yes** — show `building baseline` with a count of weeks remaining. |
| 6 | Mon–Sun, or does anyone want month? | **Mon–Sun**, matching "Monday morning". |
| 7 | Can one account's locations span timezones? | **No** — schema has only `accounts.timezone`. A 15-location group plausibly spans zones; the model cannot express it. |
| 8 | Is the 2-month gap to wall clock pipeline lag or an export artifact? | **Artifact.** Anchor on `MAX(occurred_at)`; always label the period. |

---

## 3. How each data finding is handled

| Finding | Handling |
|---|---|
| **12 exact duplicates**, 7 accounts, 11 location-weeks | Dedupe **view** over the raw table (`GROUP BY` all columns but `id`, keep `MIN(id)`). Seed untouched, all reads through it. Overcount is negligible account-wide but 1–50% (median 12%) per location-week, and every one lands in a complete week. |
| **Acct 6, `2026-06-03`, 805 events in a day** | Cause undetermined — bulk import and real demand fit equally. Handled so the answer doesn't matter: trimmed mean removes it from neighbouring baselines, and it is still flagged `above normal` in its own week. |
| **Account 20 — zero events** | HTTP 200, populated window, `insufficient_history`. Never 404, never divide by zero. Also proves the cutoff is global: a per-account `MAX` is undefined here. |
| **Per-account staleness** (acct 8 ends Jul 24, acct 2 Jul 26) | Reinforces the same rule — the window end is the dataset-wide max, so a quiet tail reads as low counts, not as a shorter window. |
| **Timezones** (6 zones, incl. `America/Phoenix` no-DST and literal `UTC`) | `week_buckets` dimension, below. 8 events change week under UTC bucketing — the direct test. |
| **Partial weeks** | `week_buckets.is_complete`. Both edge buckets are 1/7 days for all 20 accounts. Never compared, never in a baseline, never the default view. |
| **NULL outcome** (398, 3.2%) | Valid state. Counted in totals, rendered `unspecified`, never dropped. |
| **Outcome vocabulary** | 7 values, not the 5 in `docs/`, and **per-type**: calls → connected/missed/voicemail, appointments → completed/no_show, leads → converted/open. |
| **`duration_seconds`** | Noise — calls only, clamped [20,1500], uncorrelated with outcome. No metric built on it. |
| **Low volumes** (49/69 locations under 8/week) | The λ ≥ 3.7 gate and `not enough volume`. |
| **`created_at` is not the start of history** | Window comes from the data, never from `created_at`. |
| **Hour-of-day is a generator artifact** | No hour-of-day feature. |
| **Cutoff is stale and is a Monday** | Anchor on `MAX(occurred_at)`; render the period as an explicit date range. |

---

## 4. Architecture

**.NET 10 LTS** · EF Core 10 · SQL Server in Docker · Angular via current CLI (unpinned) · xUnit.

### Solution structure — three projects

```
Api    ASP.NET Core Web API. Endpoints, DTOs, DI, the aggregation SQL.
Core   Pure logic, no EF and no ASP.NET: week buckets, Poisson CDF/tails,
       trimmed mean, bands, verdicts. This is what makes unit tests infra-free.
Tests  xUnit. Unit tests over Core; integration tests over Api + Testcontainers.
```

No extra layers — no repository interface over EF, no service/manager tier, no MediatR.

**Conventions** (layout, naming, `Directory.Build.props`, test setup) come from my existing
project at `C:\src\demos\VerusLLC`. **T0 extracts them into `CLAUDE.md` first; scaffolding then
follows `CLAUDE.md`, not the reference project.** The reference is not read again after T0.

### Timezone strategy — a `week_buckets` dimension

```
week_buckets(timezone, week_start_local, utc_start, utc_end, is_complete)
```

Generated by a seeder using `TimeZoneInfo` for the 6 timezones present across the observation
window. Aggregation is a range join on an indexed `occurred_at`:

```
JOIN week_buckets b ON b.timezone = a.timezone
                   AND e.occurred_at >= b.utc_start
                   AND e.occurred_at <  b.utc_end
```

Chosen over `AT TIME ZONE` because it materialises `is_complete` as a column rather than repeating
a predicate at every call site, computes DST from .NET's tz database (which the golden tests pin),
and is independently testable. SQL Server on Linux would accept IANA names directly, so this is a
preference, not a necessity — T0 confirms `TimeZoneInfo` resolves IANA IDs and moves on.

### ORM vs raw SQL

- **EF Core** for schema, migrations (`dotnet ef migrations add`; never `EnsureCreated`), and the
  seed import.
- **Raw parameterised SQL** via `Database.SqlQueryRaw<T>` for the aggregation. That query is the
  product and must be reviewable; LINQ over a range join plus `GROUPING SETS` would not translate
  cleanly. No Dapper — not worth a second data-access library for one query.
- Account row and location rows come from **one statement** using `GROUPING SETS`.

### Endpoints

| Method | Route | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/accounts` | Account picker. |
| `GET` | `/api/accounts/{id}/pulse?week=YYYY-MM-DD` | **The aggregation.** Defaults to the last complete week. Returns the period, account verdict, and location rows ranked by tail probability — each with count, λ, band, p, verdict, per-type split. |

No write endpoints.

### Persisted user input

**Selected account and week live in the URL** (`/accounts/6/week/2026-06-01`), owned by the Angular
router. Reloading, bookmarking, or pasting the link to an account manager all restore the exact
view. That is the input whose state survives reload.

### Angular state

Signals plus one service. No NgRx: one screen, one resource.

---

## 5. Tasks and time boxes

~1h is already spent on profiling and planning. Implementation budget is **4h15 including buffer**.

| # | Task | Box |
|---|---|---|
| T0 | Extract VerusLLC conventions into `CLAUDE.md`; scaffold Api/Core/Tests from it; SQL Server up; confirm `TimeZoneInfo` resolves IANA IDs | 25m |
| T1 | EF migrations (accounts, activity_events, dedupe view, week_buckets); bucket generator; seed import | 40m |
| T2 | Core: Poisson CDF/tails, trimmed mean, bands, verdicts. Aggregation SQL + `/pulse` | 65m |
| T3 | Tests: unit over Core, integration goldens over `/pulse` | 45m |
| T4 | Angular: account picker, week navigation, ranked location table | 45m |
| T5 | README — decisions, trade-offs, how to run, what's missing | 15m |
| — | Buffer | 20m |
| | **Total** | **4h15** |

### Stop rule

1. **Per task:** overrun the box by >50% → take the fallback and move on. Do not debug into the
   next box.
2. **At 2h30**, T0–T2 must be green against the §6 goldens. If not, cut T4 to a single static table
   with no week navigation, and ship that.
3. **At 3h45**, stop feature work and write the README whatever the state. An honest gap costs less
   than a broken feature.
4. **Hard stop 4h15.**
5. **Never cut:** the dedupe view, the complete/partial distinction, the empty-account path, exact
   Poisson tails, and T5.

---

## 6. Test strategy

**What matters, in order:** (1) bucketing lands events in the right account-local week; (2) partial
weeks are excluded everywhere; (3) the trimmed mean neutralises the spike; (4) bands are never
negative; (5) dedupe applies on every read path; (6) empty and low-volume accounts degrade
gracefully. Verdict wording and UI layout get no test budget.

**Where the goldens come from.** `tools/profile_seed.py` — an independent implementation, in
another language, written before any app code. `--dedupe` reproduces what the API should serve. A
failing test is re-derived from the profiler, never "fixed" by pasting what C# returned.

| Assertion | Golden |
|---|---|
| Rows raw → deduped | 12,626 → **12,614** (12 groups, 7 accounts, 11 location-weeks) |
| Window shape, every account | 27 buckets, **25 complete**, last complete `2026-07-20`; both partial buckets 1/7 days |
| Account totals, last complete week | 1=**53**, 6=**87**, 8=**7**, 18=**20**, 19=**13**, 20=**0** |
| Acct 1 per-location, same week | A=9, B=10, C=9, D=9, E=9, F=7 |
| Trimmed mean | acct 6 baseline for `2026-06-08`: plain 138.0 → **trimmed 72.3** |
| **Spike does not poison its neighbour** | acct 6 `2026-06-08`, n=102 → **normal**; with a plain mean it would read `below normal`. Regression test for the whole baseline design. |
| Spike detected in its own week | acct 6 `2026-06-01`: λ=72.1, band [56,95], n=880 → `above normal` |
| Poisson band values | λ=3→[0,8], λ=6→[2,13], λ=25→[16,39], λ=75→[59,98] |
| **Band non-negativity** | property test over λ ∈ [0.1, 500]: `lo ≥ 0 && hi ≥ lo` always |
| Drop-to-zero floor | n=0 flags below iff λ > 3.69 |
| Dedupe at grain | acct 6 / Site E / `2026-02-23`: 3 → **2** |
| **Timezone correctness** | exactly **8** events change week under UTC bucketing (accts 1:2, 3:1, 6:1, 9:2, 12:2). Asserted as an inequality — UTC bucketing must give a different answer. |

| Ranking | default week, acct 15: Site B ranks above Site A despite neither being flagged |

**Layering:** Core tests need **zero infrastructure** and always run. Integration tests use
Testcontainers and skip with a clear message when Docker is absent, so `dotnet test` is green
either way.

### End-to-end verification

1. `docker compose up -d` → `dotnet ef database update` → import seed.
2. `dotnet test` — Core green always; integration green with Docker, skipped without.
3. `GET /api/accounts/1/pulse` → 53 for `2026-07-20`, six location rows ranked by p, nothing flagged.
4. `GET /api/accounts/6/pulse?week=2026-06-01` → 880, `above normal`, 18 locations flagged.
5. `GET /api/accounts/6/pulse?week=2026-06-08` → 102, **normal** (the trimmed-mean regression).
6. `GET /api/accounts/20/pulse` → 200, empty state.
7. SPA: navigate to `/accounts/6/week/2026-06-01`, **hard-reload** → same view restored from the URL.
8. Cross-check any figure against `python tools/profile_seed.py --dedupe`.

---

## 7. Explicitly deferred

**Out of scope per ticket/constraints:** auth, alerting and notifications, ML/forecasting, infra
and CI, visual polish.

| Deferred | Why |
|---|---|
| **Review state / "mark reviewed"** | Nobody asked for it. The persisted input is account + week in the URL. |
| **Quasi-Poisson dispersion φ** | φ ≈ 1 on this data, so its value cannot be demonstrated here. It is the first thing to add against real, overdispersed data. |
| Charts / sparklines | With Fano ≈ 1 there is no trend to read; a 25-week sparkline invites customers to find meaning in noise. |
| Per-event-type detection | Multiplies the comparisons problem on already-small counts. Needs §2.2 answered. |
| Seasonality, holidays, day-of-week modelling | Mon–Sun buckets absorb the weekday effect (weekend runs at 27% of a weekday). 26 weeks supports no more. |
| Multiplicity correction across locations | At 0.49 flags/week it is not yet the binding constraint. Revisit if locations per account grow. |
| Peer/industry benchmarking | Different product. |
| Materialised rollups | 12.6k rows; the range join is instant. Scaling path noted in the README. |
| Per-location timezones | Schema cannot express it (§2.7). |
| Pagination, i18n, full a11y audit | Max 15 locations. Semantic HTML and labels only. |

---

## Risks & notes

**The default week is empty, and that is the biggest presentation risk.** With the corrected model,
the last complete week flags **zero** accounts and **zero** locations across the entire dataset;
`2026-06-01` flags 3 and 18. Anyone opening the app at its default lands on a page where nothing is
flagged and may read correct behaviour as a broken feature. Two mitigations, both load-bearing
rather than cosmetic: the location list always ranks by tail probability so the most unusual site
is at the top even when nothing crosses a threshold, and the README opens with a direct link to
`/accounts/6/week/2026-06-01`. I would rather ship a page that is honestly quiet than one tuned to
look busy, but the quietness needs explaining on arrival.

**"Monday morning" carries an unnamed ingestion dependency.** The promise only holds if ingestion
completed through Sunday night in each account's timezone. In this seed the newest bucket is one
day old and the data is two months stale. If the real pipeline lags, the page will confidently show
a week-old verdict labelled as current. The period is therefore always rendered as an explicit date
range, and pipeline freshness is a prerequisite nobody has costed.

**Without alerting, the value is capped.** A customer only benefits if they log in on the right
morning. The most valuable version of this feature is an email saying "Site C was unusual last
week". Everything here is built so that alerting can sit on top unchanged: the tail probability is
already the ranking key and would be the trigger.

**The dedupe view does not survive scale.** A SQL Server view with `GROUP BY` cannot be indexed, so
this pattern is right for 12.6k rows and wrong for millions — production should reject duplicates
at ingest with a unique constraint on the natural key. A view also hides the problem rather than
fixing it: whatever produces those 12 rows keeps producing them. The README says so.

**The model is calibrated on synthetic data.** Fano ≈ 1 means this seed has no seasonality,
campaigns, or holidays. Real data will be overdispersed and the bands will be too tight — more
false flags than the 0.49/week measured here. That is what the deferred φ parameter is for, and it
is the first thing I would add once real data existed to fit it against.

**The deliverable is deliberately quieter than the ticket implies.** "Comparing against some
baseline" reads naturally as a trend line, which this data cannot support. I am building a verdict,
a typical range, and silence — a page that says "normal" most weeks is the feature working.

```
JOIN week_buckets b ON b.timezone = a.timezone
                   AND e.occurred_at >= b.utc_start
                   AND e.occurred_at <  b.utc_end
```

Chosen over `AT TIME ZONE` because it materialises `is_complete` as a column rather than repeating
a predicate at every call site, computes DST from .NET's tz database (which the golden tests pin),
and is independently testable. SQL Server on Linux would accept IANA names directly, so this is a
preference, not a necessity — T0 confirms `TimeZoneInfo` resolves IANA IDs and moves on.

### ORM vs raw SQL

- **EF Core** for schema, migrations (`dotnet ef migrations add`; never `EnsureCreated`), and the
  seed import.
- **Raw parameterised SQL** via `Database.SqlQueryRaw<T>` for the aggregation. That query is the
  product and must be reviewable; LINQ over a range join plus `GROUPING SETS` would not translate
  cleanly. No Dapper — not worth a second data-access library for one query.
- Account row and location rows come from **one statement** using `GROUPING SETS`.

| Method | Route | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/accounts` | Account picker. |
| `GET` | `/api/accounts/{id}/pulse?week=YYYY-MM-DD` | **The aggregation.** Defaults to the last complete week. Returns the period, account verdict, and location rows ranked by tail probability — each with count, λ, band, p, verdict, per-type split. |

No write endpoints.

**Selected account and week live in the URL** (`/accounts/6/week/2026-06-01`), owned by the Angular
router. Reloading, bookmarking, or pasting the link to an account manager all restore the exact
view. That is the input whose state survives reload.

### Angular state

Signals plus one service. No NgRx: one screen, one resource.

All three applied.

**1. AI log.** T5 is now "README + AI log" at 35m (export transcripts, review `decisions.md` for accuracy and gaps, write `ai-log/reflection.md`); buffer cut to 15m. **New total: 4h30** — that's 15m above the 4h15 cap you set last round, since +20m on T5 minus 5m of buffer. Flagging rather than silently absorbing it; if 4h15 is hard, T4 (Angular, 45m) is the box I'd take it from. I also shifted the stop-rule checkpoints to stay coherent: "start T5" moves 3h45 → 3h55, hard stop 4h15 → 4h30.

**2. IANA claim.** Removed and replaced with the correct statement — SQL Server normalizes to Windows zone names on Linux as well as Windows, so `AT TIME ZONE` is out regardless of host OS. That actually strengthens the `week_buckets` rationale: it's now a necessity, not a preference.

**3. Plain-language likelihood.** Added a "Presentation" row to the §1 table and a short "How this reads on screen" subsection with a copy table. `N = round(1/p)`, translated by a pure function in `Core` so the wording is unit-tested and the SPA holds no statistics. Endpoint description now says `p` is for clients and tests only.

One sub-decision inside (3) worth your eye: **flagged rows quote the threshold, unflagged rows quote the rounded frequency.** So a flagged drop reads "less than 1 in 40 times" rather than "1 in 43" — the exact figure would imply more precision than a 12-week baseline supports. But the top-ranked row in a quiet week needs the actual number to be readable at all ("roughly 1 week in 30 is this quiet"), which is what makes the empty default week informative rather than blank.
